payload.angle: The honest answer, made usable from Australia. It closes with the invisible work of a French wedding week that an advisor coordinates.

Religious ceremonies: civil must come first in France (several ranking pages and the US Embassy say so; research to confirm from service-public.gouv.fr).

outline.h2: Can foreigners marry legally in France?
outline.answers: The short honest answer in the first 60 words, and which of two routes applies to you.
must_include: Direct answer: a legal marriage in France takes place at the mairie and requires a residence link to the commune (at least one partner French or legally resident, per the run-log decision; research batch to supply exact wording, period and source).
Only the civil ceremony at the mairie is legally binding in France (Australian Embassy France).

Two routes in a short comparison table: legal in France (who qualifies) vs legal in Australia plus celebration in France. Columns: who it suits, where the legal part happens, extra paperwork, what the French day looks like.
Use 'getting married in france' naturally in this section.
House line: requirements change and mairies apply them differently; confirm with the mairie and for your own passports.

outline.h2: Residency and eligibility: who qualifies for a French civil wedding
outline.answers: What 'residence' means, how long, how it is proven, and what does not count.
must_include: Residence or domicile of at least one partner (or a parent, if official sources say so) in the commune, the minimum period, and proof accepted. From service-public.gouv.fr and the Australian Embassy France only; do not use the competitor figures.
Holiday stays and short-stay visa-free entry do not make residency unless an official source says otherwise (research).
Same-sex couples: marriage open to same-sex couples in France (research to confirm source and any nationality condition).
No immigration advice.

Livret de famille and the French marriage certificate.

outline.answers: What you can hold in France without the legal step, and the rule for religious weddings.
